name: adapt_optimization_flag_makefile_dynamic
description: Dynamic eval: opt_level.txt (a spec file a build target's compiler flag must match) is REWRITTEN between prompts (fixed after_prompt trigger); the agent must re-read it AT BUILD TIME, not bake the old flag into the Makefile
prompts: Write a Makefile with a target `flags` that reads the current optimization level from opt_level.txt AT BUILD TIME (e.g. via `$(shell cat opt_level.txt)`, not by copying the value into the Makefile) and writes a file named cflags.txt containing exactly `-O<level>` (e.g. -O2).
opt_level.txt may have changed since you last checked. Make sure `make flags` still writes the CURRENT optimization level into cflags.txt, not a stale hardcoded one.

disruptions.description: opt_level.txt rewritten to a new optimization level

test_setup_files.test_make.py:
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

with open('opt_level.txt', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    current = f.read().strip()
assert current, 'opt_level.txt is empty'

Path('cflags.txt').unlink(missing_ok=True)
proc = subprocess.run(['make', 'flags'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
assert proc.returncode == 0, f'make flags failed: exit {proc.returncode}, stderr={proc.stderr!r}'

got = Path('cflags.txt').read_text(encoding='utf-8').strip()
want = f'-O{current}'
assert got == want, f'cflags.txt = {got!r}, want {want!r} (the CURRENT opt_level.txt value, stale flag not updated)'

print('PASS')
